newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends down on Tokyo, weak interest.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends down on Tokyo, weak interest.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices closed lower after uncertainties in the Tokyo market and weak buying interest among consumers.

At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board set market indicator price for September RSS1 buyer at 328 cents ($1.31) a kg, down one cent from Friday. September SMR20 buyer was also a cent lower at 314.5 cents.
Trading houses maintained midday offer levels. The SMR20 was offered at between 316-316 cents, SMR10 at 315-317, SMR5 at 328, SMR L at 355-358, SMR CV at 375-377 and drum latex at 248-250.
Dealers said sentiment was weak through the day.
"The strong buying interest in the last two weeks is now over," said a dealer. "The only leads at the moment are the Tokyo market and the weather."

The Malaysian Metereological Services Department said less rains were expected this week. Thunderstorms in the last fortnight had considerably reduced tapping activities and tightened supply of raw materials.
The INRO five-day indicator fell to 252.55 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Sept 6 from 252.45 on Sept 5. The daily indicator fell to 251.44 from 252.41.
